встречаться.gloss: to meet; to date, go out

meanings.en: to date, go out with each other
meanings.note: Мы встречаемся = we're dating. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to meet; to date, go out', paired with 'встретиться'.

meanings.en: to meet up, see each other
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to meet; to date, go out', paired with 'встретиться'.

examples.trans: We've been going out for a month already.

examples.text: Мы уже месяц встречаемся. Мне надоело уже.
examples.trans: We've been going out for a month already. I'm tired of it already.

Своя девушка. Common feminine noun meaning 'young woman; girlfriend' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('living, alive, live').

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'метить'). Used in Russian as a perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to notice', forming an aspectual pair with 'замечать'.

examples.trans: He did not notice the loss.

examples.text: Никто на кухне ничего не заметил.
examples.trans: Nobody in the kitchen noticed anything.
And what if someone notices me?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, pretty, handsome').

examples.text: Красивая. Но это же не ваша жена! Я вашу жену видел.
examples.trans: She's pretty. But that's not your wife! I've seen your wife.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('best; better').

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: мам! = casual 'Mum!' when calling her

нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'врать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'lied'.

examples.text: Макс, я же тебе поверил, а ты наврал даже мне!
examples.trans: Max, I believed you, and you lied even to me!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и наврать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and lied on time.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!
examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone about this, okay?
But legally you are nobody to her.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Once. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'целовать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to kiss', paired with 'целовать'.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!

meanings.note: 'на работе' = at work. Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
